counterexample.constraintsExplanation: n=10 is in 2..100 and exactly n initial vote counts lie in 1..1000. Each bribe transfers one rival vote to Limak. Strictly more than every rival, not a tie, is required.
counterexample.mathematicalDerivation: With 1 bribes Limak has 6, requiring all rivals <= 5; at least 3 votes must be removed from rivals, more than 1. For fewer bribes this required removal only increases, so none can suffice. With 2 bribes Limak has 7, mandatory removals to reach rival cap 6 total 2. The certificate gives nonnegative transfers [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0], total 2, producing rivals [3, 4, 5, 5, 2, 1, 6, 4, 1], whose maximum 6 is strictly smaller than 7. Thus the minimum is 2.
